correctness.rationale: Writing r=exp(hν/(kBT)) and u=1/(r+1) reduces the normalized component colors to (u,u³/(1−2u+2u²)). First-band intensity contributions give positive barycentric weights. The differentiated curve is strictly convex and u/2−f(u)=u(1−2u)/(2(1−2u+2u²)) is strictly positive on the allowed domain, giving the equality and unattained-bound claims. At fixed U the chord between t and 1/2−t varies continuously from upper-line height U/2 to f(U). At U=1/4 both endpoints tend to U and the weights stay 1/2; the lower limit holds by continuity, not by one weight tending to one as in the noncentral case. Inverting each endpoint and setting its c proportional to its barycentric weight times (r−1) gives distinct finite positive temperatures, positive amplitudes, and the exact first-band normalization. One band pair at fixed β is always reproducible by one temperature. With free β the separate single-component quotient is (r+1)/(r²+1)<1, and the frozen two-temperature example gives 3187075/2993536>1 by exact fractions. The script was inspected, not run; these checks establish the result analytically, not through finite sampling.
